idiom_name: sealed record node types (positional properties) + switch expression
implementation_notes: Records declare the named children as positional properties in one line per node type, and switch expressions with type and property patterns implement node-specific operations without visitor scaffolding: match Binary b and read b.Left, b.Right directly. Prefer it for C# 9+ compiler front ends where nodes are data and operations are functions; keep the classic class hierarchy when nodes own behaviour or must remain mutable.
pitfalls: Records synthesise structural equality and GetHashCode that recurse through every positional member - expensive on large trees and wrong when nodes carry position metadata or share subtrees.
A switch expression needs a discard arm to be exhaustive; without _ => throw, a newly added node type falls through silently.

variants.name: Abstract class nodes with named properties
variants.idiom_name: abstract Expr + sealed node classes with named properties
variants.implementation_notes: The classic form works directly in C#: an abstract Expr plus sealed node classes whose named child properties are the structure, dispatched through virtual methods. C# 7 type patterns already remove most casts in visitors (case Binary b:), so this form stays practical when nodes carry behaviour or when the codebase follows the compiler-style hierarchy - Roslyn's syntax classes expose exactly these named child accessors.
pitfalls: Pattern matching over an open class hierarchy is not exhaustive: the compiler cannot prove that all node types are covered, so a discard arm that throws is the only guard.
Mutable child properties let callers break the arity invariant after construction; prefer get-only or init-only properties.
